D.3 Proof of Proposition 2

We first describe the hard instance construction before stating the formal separation result and proof.

Hard instance setup.

Fix a target constant c>1c>1 and choose parameters k≥2​ck\geq\sqrt{2c} and δ∈(0,1)\delta\in(0,1) with δ≥1−12​c\delta\geq 1-\tfrac{1}{2c}. For any ε∈(0,14​k2]\varepsilon\in(0,\tfrac{1}{4k^{2}}], define α:=k​ε\alpha:=k\sqrt{\varepsilon} and M:=1/αM:=1/\alpha, and let the reference distribution πref\pi_{\mathrm{ref}} be supported on three outcomes {B,C,P}\{B,C,P\} with masses

πref​(B)=1−α,πref​(C)=α−ε,πref​(P)=ε,\displaystyle\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(B)=1-\alpha,\qquad\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(C)=\alpha-\varepsilon,\qquad\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(P)=\varepsilon, (227)

so ε<α≤1/2\varepsilon<\alpha\leq 1/2 for all ε≤14​k2\varepsilon\leq\tfrac{1}{4k^{2}}). Define the score function r^:{B,C,P}→[0,1]\hat{r}:\{B,C,P\}\to[0,1] by

r^​(B)=0,r^​(C)=1−δ,r^​(P)=1,\displaystyle\hat{r}(B)=0,\qquad\hat{r}(C)=1-\delta,\qquad\hat{r}(P)=1, (228)

and the true reward r⋆:{B,C,P}→[0,1]r^{\star}:\{B,C,P\}\to[0,1] by

r⋆​(B)=12,r⋆​(C)=1,r⋆​(P)=0.\displaystyle r^{\star}(B)=\tfrac{1}{2},\qquad r^{\star}(C)=1,\qquad r^{\star}(P)=0. (229)

Recall for reward function rr the pairwise outcome

ϕr(y,y′)=𝟏{r(y)>r(y′)}+12 1{r(y)=r(y′)},\displaystyle\phi_{r}(y,y^{\prime})=\mathbf{1}\{r(y)>r(y^{\prime})\}+\frac{1}{2}\,\mathbf{1}\{r(y)=r(y^{\prime})\}, (230)

and the pairwise reward-model error

εpw=𝔼y,y′∼πref​[|ϕr^​(y,y′)−ϕr⋆​(y,y′)|].\displaystyle\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}}=\mathbb{E}_{y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}\left[|\phi_{\widehat{r}}(y,y^{\prime})-\phi_{r^{\star}}(y,y^{\prime})|\right]. (231)

In our construction, r^\hat{r} and r⋆r^{\star} induce no ties except when y=y′y=y^{\prime}, in which case ϕr^​(y,y′)=ϕr⋆​(y,y′)=12\phi_{\hat{r}}(y,y^{\prime})=\phi_{r^{\star}}(y,y^{\prime})=\tfrac{1}{2}; hence |ϕr^(y,y′)−ϕr⋆(y,y′)|=𝟏{ϕr^(y,y′)≠ϕr⋆(y,y′)}|\phi_{\hat{r}}(y,y^{\prime})-\phi_{r^{\star}}(y,y^{\prime})|=\mathbf{1}\{\phi_{\hat{r}}(y,y^{\prime})\neq\phi_{r^{\star}}(y,y^{\prime})\}. Since r^​(B)<r^​(C)<r^​(P)\widehat{r}(B)<\widehat{r}(C)<\widehat{r}(P) while r⋆​(P)<r⋆​(B)<r⋆​(C)r^{\star}(P)<r^{\star}(B)<r^{\star}(C), the only strict-order disagreements occur exactly when one draw is PP and the other is in {B,C}\{B,C\}. Therefore,

εpw=ℙ⁡(y=P,y′≠P)+ℙ⁡(y≠P,y′=P)=2​πref​(P)​(1−πref​(P))=2​ε​(1−ε).\displaystyle\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}}=\mathbb{P}(y=P,y^{\prime}\neq P)+\mathbb{P}(y\neq P,y^{\prime}=P)=2\,\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(P)\,(1-\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(P))=2\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon). (232)

Since the above expression is increasing on (0,12)(0,\frac{1}{2}) and our setup assumes ε≤14​k2\varepsilon\leq\frac{1}{4k^{2}}, it follows that

0<εpw≤12​k2​(1−14​k2).\displaystyle 0<\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}}\leq\frac{1}{2k^{2}}\left(1-\frac{1}{4k^{2}}\right). (233)

Finally, the two policies to be compared are the top-α\alpha quantile policy under r^\widehat{r} and the family of solutions (parametrized by β\beta) to the χ2\chi^{2}-regularized variational problem.

Proof sketch.

Before stating the formal result, we first provide intuition for why this example creates a separation. The construction creates a spurious top-score spike PP of tiny reference mass ε\varepsilon that looks best under r^\hat{r} but is worst under r⋆r^{\star}, alongside a near-top outcome CC of mass α−ε\alpha-\varepsilon that is truly optimal. The πM\pi_{M} must spread its mass over P∪CP\cup C, so it only pays a regret proportional to the unavoidable contamination fraction ε/α\varepsilon/\alpha. In contrast, the χ2\chi^{2}-regularized solution reweights proportionally to the score gap (r^−λ)+(\hat{r}-\lambda)_{+}, so it overconcentrates on the spike PP whenever PP has even a slight score advantage over CC (controlled by δ\delta), inducing an additional regret term that cannot be tuned away uniformly over β\beta. Thus, in order to increase the constant factor win-rate regret gap between the two policies prescribed by a fixed cc, we would like to increase the score gap by decreasing δ\delta and increasing the total-mass of the top-quantile α\alpha, both as a function of cc.

Proposition 5.

For every target constant c>1c>1, there exist (k,δ)(k,\delta) with k≥2​ck\geq\sqrt{2c} and δ≥1−12​c\delta\geq 1-\tfrac{1}{2c}, and an εpw0=εpw0​(k)\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}_{0}}=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}_{0}}(k) defined by εpw0:=12​k2​(1−14​k2)\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}_{0}}:=\tfrac{1}{2k^{2}}(1-\tfrac{1}{4k^{2}}), such that for every εpw∈(0,εpw0]\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}}\in(0,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}_{0}}], there exists a hard instance of the form in the above setup for which

infβ>0Rr⋆​(π⋆)−Rr⋆​(πβχ)≥c⋅(infM>0Rr⋆​(π⋆)−Rr⋆​(πM)).\displaystyle\inf_{\beta>0}R^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\star})-R^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta})\geq c\cdot\left(\inf_{M>0}R^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\star})-R^{r^{\star}}(\pi_{M})\right). (234)

The range for εpw\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}} above is implied by the constraint ε≤14​k2\varepsilon\leq\tfrac{1}{4k^{2}} based on our construction. Moreover, for any target εpw∈(0,εpw0]\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}}\in(0,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}_{0}}] we may choose the unique ε\varepsilon obtained by inverting (232). Since εpw≍ε\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}}\asymp\varepsilon, achieving larger cc requires choosing smaller ε\varepsilon (hence smaller εpw\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}}) to keep α=k​ε≤12\alpha=k\sqrt{\varepsilon}\leq\tfrac{1}{2}. In the proof below, we first solve for the explicit form of each policy before comparing performance and concluding a separation result.

Proof.

Fix β>0\beta>0. Recall from Huang et al. [14] that the χ2\chi^{2}-regularized solution admits the pointwise form

πβχ​(y)=πref​(y)​wβ​(y),wβ​(y):=relu⁡(β−1​(r^​(y)−λ))=(r^​(y)−λ)+β,\displaystyle\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}(y)\;=\;\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(y)\,w_{\beta}(y),\qquad w_{\beta}(y)\;:=\;\mathrm{relu}\!\left(\beta^{-1}(\widehat{r}(y)-\lambda)\right)\;=\;\frac{(\widehat{r}(y)-\lambda)_{+}}{\beta}, (235)

where λ\lambda is chosen so that ∑yπref​(y)​wβ​(y)=1\sum_{y}\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(y)w_{\beta}(y)=1, i.e.

𝔼y∼πref​[(r^​(y)−λ)+]=β.\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}\big[(\widehat{r}(y)-\lambda)_{+}\big]\;=\;\beta. (236)

Enforcing normalization.

For our instance, plugging in the values of r^\widehat{r} from (228) and πref\pi_{\mathrm{ref}} weights from (227), the normalization condition (236) becomes

(1−α)​(0−λ)++(α−ε)​(1−δ−λ)++ε​(1−λ)+=β.\displaystyle(1-\alpha)\,(0-\lambda)_{+}\;+\;(\alpha-\varepsilon)\,(1-\delta-\lambda)_{+}\;+\;\varepsilon\,(1-\lambda)_{+}\;=\;\beta. (237)

We will define for convenience the reference mean of r^\widehat{r} on this instance:

μ:=𝔼πref​[r^]=(α−ε)​(1−δ)+ε=α⁡(1−δ)+ε​δ.\displaystyle\mu\;:=\;\mathbb{E}_{\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}[\widehat{r}]\;=\;(\alpha-\varepsilon)(1-\delta)\;+\;\varepsilon\;=\;\alpha(1-\delta)+\varepsilon\delta. (238)

Solving for λ⁡(β)\lambda(\beta).

Before calculating an explicit form of πβχ\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}, we identify three λ\lambda regimes for the policy based on the values of β\beta. We solve (237) by cases, according to where λ\lambda falls relative to 00, 1−δ1-\delta, and 11.

Case I: λ∈[1−δ, 1)\lambda\in[1-\delta,\,1). Then (1−δ−λ)+=0(1-\delta-\lambda)_{+}=0 and (0−λ)+=0(0-\lambda)_{+}=0, while (1−λ)+=1−λ(1-\lambda)_{+}=1-\lambda, so

β=ε⁡(1−λ)⟹λ= 1−β/ε.\displaystyle\beta=\varepsilon(1-\lambda)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\lambda\;=\;1-\beta/\varepsilon. (239)

This case is self-consistent iff λ≥1−δ\lambda\geq 1-\delta, i.e. 1−β/ε≥1−δ1-\beta/\varepsilon\geq 1-\delta equivalently

β≤ε​δ.\displaystyle\beta\leq\varepsilon\delta. (240)

Case II: λ∈[0, 1−δ)\lambda\in[0,\,1-\delta). Then (0−λ)+=0(0-\lambda)_{+}=0, while both (1−δ−λ)+=1−δ−λ(1-\delta-\lambda)_{+}=1-\delta-\lambda and (1−λ)+=1−λ(1-\lambda)_{+}=1-\lambda, so

β=(α−ε)​(1−δ−λ)+ε⁡(1−λ)=μ−α​λ.\displaystyle\beta=(\alpha-\varepsilon)(1-\delta-\lambda)+\varepsilon(1-\lambda)=\mu-\alpha\lambda. (241)

Hence

λ=μ−βα.\displaystyle\lambda\;=\;\frac{\mu-\beta}{\alpha}. (242)

Self-consistency requires λ<1−δ\lambda<1-\delta and λ≥0\lambda\geq 0. The first is

μ−βα<1−δ⟺μ−β<α⁡(1−δ)⟺β>μ−α⁡(1−δ)=ε​δ,\displaystyle\frac{\mu-\beta}{\alpha}<1-\delta\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\mu-\beta<\alpha(1-\delta)\;\Longleftrightarrow\;\beta>\mu-\alpha(1-\delta)=\varepsilon\delta, (243)

and the second is μ−β≥0⇔β≤μ\mu-\beta\geq 0\iff\beta\leq\mu. So Case II holds for

ε​δ<β≤μ.\displaystyle\varepsilon\delta\;<\;\beta\;\leq\;\mu. (244)

Case III: λ<0\lambda<0. Then all three ReLU terms are active: (0−λ)+=−λ(0-\lambda)_{+}=-\lambda, (1−δ−λ)+=1−δ−λ(1-\delta-\lambda)_{+}=1-\delta-\lambda, (1−λ)+=1−λ(1-\lambda)_{+}=1-\lambda, so

β=(1−α)​(−λ)+(α−ε)​(1−δ−λ)+ε⁡(1−λ)=μ−λ.\displaystyle\beta=(1-\alpha)(-\lambda)+(\alpha-\varepsilon)(1-\delta-\lambda)+\varepsilon(1-\lambda)=\mu-\lambda. (245)

Self-consistency λ<0\lambda<0 is exactly

β>μ.\displaystyle\beta>\mu. (246)

Finding the explicit form of πβχ\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}.

Recall πβχ=πref⋅wβ\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}=\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}\cdot w_{\beta} with

wβ​(y)=(r^​(y)−λ)+β,\displaystyle w_{\beta}(y)=\frac{(\widehat{r}(y)-\lambda)_{+}}{\beta}, (247)

and λ=λ⁡(β)\lambda=\lambda(\beta) given by the previous case analysis. We now record the resulting πβχ\pi^{\chi}_{\beta} in each β\beta-regime.

Regime I (β≤ε​δ\beta\leq\varepsilon\delta): here λ=1−β/ε∈[1−δ,1)\lambda=1-\beta/\varepsilon\in[1-\delta,1), so only PP is active:

wβ​(P)=1−λβ=β/εβ=1ε,\displaystyle w_{\beta}(P)=\frac{1-\lambda}{\beta}=\frac{\beta/\varepsilon}{\beta}=\frac{1}{\varepsilon}, (248)

while wβ​(C)=wβ​(B)=0w_{\beta}(C)=w_{\beta}(B)=0. Thus

πβχ​(P)=1,πβχ​(C)=0,πβχ​(B)=0.\displaystyle\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}(P)=1,\qquad\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}(C)=0,\qquad\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}(B)=0. (249)

Regime II (ε​δ<β≤μ\varepsilon\delta<\beta\leq\mu): here λ=(μ−β)/α∈[0,1−δ)\lambda=(\mu-\beta)/\alpha\in[0,1-\delta), so BB is inactive and C,PC,P are active:

wβ​(C)=1−δ−λβ=β−ε​δα​β,wβ​(P)=1−λβ=α−μ+βα​β.\displaystyle w_{\beta}(C)=\frac{1-\delta-\lambda}{\beta}=\frac{\beta-\varepsilon\delta}{\alpha\beta},\qquad w_{\beta}(P)=\frac{1-\lambda}{\beta}=\frac{\alpha-\mu+\beta}{\alpha\beta}. (250)

Therefore

πβχ​(B)=0,πβχ​(C)=(α−ε)​(β−ε​δα​β),πβχ​(P)=ε⁡(α−μ+βα​β).\displaystyle\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}(B)=0,\qquad\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}(C)=(\alpha-\varepsilon)\left(\frac{\beta-\varepsilon\delta}{\alpha\beta}\right),\qquad\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}(P)=\varepsilon\left(\frac{\alpha-\mu+\beta}{\alpha\beta}\right). (251)

Regime III (β>μ\beta>\mu): here λ=μ−β<0\lambda=\mu-\beta<0, so all three actions are active. For BB and CC we have

wβ​(B)=−λβ=1−μβ,wβ​(C)=1−δ−λβ=1+(1−δ)−μβ,\displaystyle w_{\beta}(B)=\frac{-\lambda}{\beta}=1-\frac{\mu}{\beta},\qquad w_{\beta}(C)=\frac{1-\delta-\lambda}{\beta}=1+\frac{(1-\delta)-\mu}{\beta}, (252)

and for PP we have

wβ​(P)=1−λβ=1+1−μβ.\displaystyle w_{\beta}(P)=\frac{1-\lambda}{\beta}=1+\frac{1-\mu}{\beta}. (253)

Therefore, for BB and CC,

πβχ​(B)=(1−α)​(1−μβ),πβχ​(C)=(α−ε)​(1+(1−δ)−μβ),\displaystyle\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}(B)=(1-\alpha)\left(1-\frac{\mu}{\beta}\right),\quad\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}(C)=(\alpha-\varepsilon)\left(1+\frac{(1-\delta)-\mu}{\beta}\right), (254)

and for PP,

πβχ​(P)=ε⁡(1+1−μβ).\displaystyle\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}(P)=\varepsilon\left(1+\frac{1-\mu}{\beta}\right). (255)

Using this explicit formulation of πβχ\pi^{\chi}_{\beta} in these three regimes, we next compute the win-rate exactly.

Computing Rr⋆​(πβχ)R^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}).

For each region t∈{B,C,P}t\in\{B,C,P\} recall the definition of win-rate as:

v⁡(t):=ℙy′∼πref​(r⋆​(t)>r⋆​(y′))+12​ℙy′∼πref​(r⋆​(t)=r⋆​(y′)).\displaystyle v(t)\;:=\;\mathbb{P}_{y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}\!\left(r^{\star}(t)>r^{\star}(y^{\prime})\right)\;+\;\frac{1}{2}\,\mathbb{P}_{y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}\!\left(r^{\star}(t)=r^{\star}(y^{\prime})\right). (256)

By construction r⋆​(C)=1r^{\star}(C)=1, r⋆​(B)=12r^{\star}(B)=\tfrac{1}{2}, r⋆​(P)=0r^{\star}(P)=0, so ties occur only when y′=ty^{\prime}=t. Hence,

v⁡(C)\displaystyle v(C) =ℙ⁡(y′∈{B,P})+12​ℙ​(y′=C)=(1−α+ε)+12​(α−ε)=1−α−ε2,\displaystyle=\mathbb{P}(y^{\prime}\in\{B,P\})+\frac{1}{2}\,\mathbb{P}(y^{\prime}=C)=(1-\alpha+\varepsilon)+\frac{1}{2}(\alpha-\varepsilon)=1-\frac{\alpha-\varepsilon}{2}, (257)
v⁡(B)\displaystyle v(B) =ℙ⁡(y′=P)+12​ℙ​(y′=B)=ε+1−α2,\displaystyle=\mathbb{P}(y^{\prime}=P)+\frac{1}{2}\,\mathbb{P}(y^{\prime}=B)=\varepsilon+\frac{1-\alpha}{2}, (258)
v⁡(P)\displaystyle v(P) =12​ℙ​(y′=P)=ε2.\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\,\mathbb{P}(y^{\prime}=P)=\frac{\varepsilon}{2}. (259)

Therefore, for any policy π\pi supported on {B,C,P}\{B,C,P\},

Rr⋆​(π)\displaystyle R^{r^{\star}}(\pi) =ℙy∼π,y′∼πref​(r⋆​(y)>r⋆​(y′))+12​ℙy∼π,y′∼πref​(r⋆​(y)=r⋆​(y′))\displaystyle=\mathbb{P}_{y\sim\pi,\,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}\!\left(r^{\star}(y)>r^{\star}(y^{\prime})\right)+\frac{1}{2}\,\mathbb{P}_{y\sim\pi,\,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}\!\left(r^{\star}(y)=r^{\star}(y^{\prime})\right) (260)
=∑t∈{B,C,P}π⁡(t)​v​(t)=π⁡(C)​v​(C)+π⁡(B)​v​(B)+π⁡(P)​v​(P).\displaystyle=\sum_{t\in\{B,C,P\}}\pi(t)\,v(t)=\pi(C)\,v(C)+\pi(B)\,v(B)+\pi(P)\,v(P). (261)

We now plug in the mass of πβχ\pi^{\chi}_{\beta} in each regime given in (249)–(254).

Regime I (β≤ε​δ\beta\leq\varepsilon\delta). Using (249) and (260), we have πβχ​(P)=1\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}(P)=1, hence

Rr⋆​(πβχ)=v⁡(P)=ε2.\displaystyle R^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta})=v(P)=\frac{\varepsilon}{2}. (262)

Regime II (ε​δ<β≤μ\varepsilon\delta<\beta\leq\mu). Here πβχ​(B)=0\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}(B)=0 by (251), so by (260),

Rr⋆​(πβχ)\displaystyle R^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}) =πβχ​(C)​v​(C)+πβχ​(P)​v​(P)\displaystyle=\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}(C)\,v(C)+\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}(P)\,v(P) (263)
=v⁡(P)+πβχ​(C)​(v⁡(C)−v⁡(P)).\displaystyle=v(P)+\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}(C)\left(v(C)-v(P)\right). (264)

With the values v⁡(P)=ε/2v(P)=\varepsilon/2 and v⁡(C)−v⁡(P)=1−α/2v(C)-v(P)=1-\alpha/2, plugging in the explicit πβχ​(C)\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}(C) from (251) yields

Rr⋆​(πβχ)=ε2+(1−α2)​(α−ε)​(β−ε​δα​β).\displaystyle R^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta})=\frac{\varepsilon}{2}+\left(1-\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)(\alpha-\varepsilon)\left(\frac{\beta-\varepsilon\delta}{\alpha\beta}\right). (265)

Regime III (β>μ\beta>\mu). Plugging in the explicit πβχ\pi^{\chi}_{\beta} from (254) into (260) yields

Rr⋆​(πβχ)\displaystyle R^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}) =(α−ε)​(1+(1−δ)−μβ)​(1−α−ε2)\displaystyle=(\alpha-\varepsilon)\left(1+\frac{(1-\delta)-\mu}{\beta}\right)\left(1-\frac{\alpha-\varepsilon}{2}\right) (266)
+(1−α)​(1−μβ)​(ε+1−α2)+ε⁡(1+1−μβ)​(ε2).\displaystyle\quad+(1-\alpha)\left(1-\frac{\mu}{\beta}\right)\left(\varepsilon+\frac{1-\alpha}{2}\right)+\varepsilon\left(1+\frac{1-\mu}{\beta}\right)\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\right). (267)

Computing Rr⋆​(πM)R^{r^{\star}}(\pi_{M}).

On this instance (with α>ε\alpha>\varepsilon), the top-α\alpha set under r^\widehat{r} is exactly {P,C}\{P,C\}, so

πM=πref(⋅∣{P,C}),πM(C)=α−εα=1−εα,πM(P)=εα,πM(B)=0.\displaystyle\pi_{M}=\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(\cdot\mid\{P,C\}),\qquad\pi_{M}(C)=\frac{\alpha-\varepsilon}{\alpha}=1-\frac{\varepsilon}{\alpha},\qquad\pi_{M}(P)=\frac{\varepsilon}{\alpha},\qquad\pi_{M}(B)=0. (268)

Using the values for v⁡(P)v(P) and v⁡(C)v(C) and plugging into (260), we obtain

Rr⋆​(πM)\displaystyle R^{r^{\star}}(\pi_{M}) =πM​(C)​v​(C)+πM​(P)​v​(P)\displaystyle=\pi_{M}(C)\,v(C)+\pi_{M}(P)\,v(P) (269)
=(1−εα)​(1−α−ε2)+εα⋅ε2.\displaystyle=\left(1-\frac{\varepsilon}{\alpha}\right)\left(1-\frac{\alpha-\varepsilon}{2}\right)+\frac{\varepsilon}{\alpha}\cdot\frac{\varepsilon}{2}. (270)

Equivalently, since v⁡(C)−v⁡(P)=1−α/2v(C)-v(P)=1-\alpha/2, this can be written more transparently as

Rr⋆​(πM)=ε2+(1−α2)​πM​(C)=ε2+(1−α2)​(1−εα),\displaystyle R^{r^{\star}}(\pi_{M})=\frac{\varepsilon}{2}+\left(1-\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)\pi_{M}(C)=\frac{\varepsilon}{2}+\left(1-\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)\left(1-\frac{\varepsilon}{\alpha}\right), (271)

Rewriting in this way will prove to be useful when comparing policies in regret. Now that we have the win-rates for each policy, we can compute the regret against the best policy on this instance.

Computing win-rate regret.

Since CC is strictly optimal under r⋆r^{\star}, we take the benchmark policy to be π⋆:=δC\pi^{\star}:=\delta_{C}. Thus,

Rr⋆​(π⋆)=Rr⋆​(δC)=v⁡(C)=1−α−ε2.\displaystyle R^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\star})=R^{r^{\star}}(\delta_{C})=v(C)=1-\frac{\alpha-\varepsilon}{2}. (272)

For compactness, we define the win-rate regret by

Reg⁡(π):=Rr⋆​(δC)−Rr⋆​(π)=v⁡(C)−Rr⋆​(π).\displaystyle\mathrm{Reg}(\pi)\;:=\;R^{r^{\star}}(\delta_{C})-R^{r^{\star}}(\pi)=v(C)-R^{r^{\star}}(\pi). (273)

Regret of πM\pi_{M}. Using (271) and v⁡(C)=1−α−ε2=1−α2+ε2v(C)=1-\frac{\alpha-\varepsilon}{2}=1-\frac{\alpha}{2}+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}, the regret of the top-quantile selector is

Reg⁡(πM)\displaystyle\mathrm{Reg}(\pi_{M}) =v⁡(C)−Rr⋆​(πM)\displaystyle=v(C)-R^{r^{\star}}(\pi_{M}) (274)
=(1−α2+ε2)−(ε2+(1−α2)​(1−εα))\displaystyle=\left(1-\frac{\alpha}{2}+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\right)-\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{2}+\left(1-\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)\left(1-\frac{\varepsilon}{\alpha}\right)\right) (275)
=(1−α2)​εα.\displaystyle=\left(1-\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)\frac{\varepsilon}{\alpha}. (276)

Regret of πβχ\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}: regime-wise. We use the regime-wise win-rate formulas (262)–(266) together with Reg⁡(π)=v⁡(C)−Rr⋆​(π)\mathrm{Reg}(\pi)=v(C)-R^{r^{\star}}(\pi).

Regime I (β≤ε​δ\beta\leq\varepsilon\delta). From (262), Rr⋆​(πβχ)=ε/2R^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta})=\varepsilon/2, hence

Reg⁡(πβχ)=v⁡(C)−ε2=1−α2.\displaystyle\mathrm{Reg}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta})=v(C)-\frac{\varepsilon}{2}=1-\frac{\alpha}{2}. (277)

Regime II (ε​δ<β≤μ\varepsilon\delta<\beta\leq\mu). From (265), Rr⋆​(πβχ)=ε2+(1−α2)​πβχ​(C)R^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta})=\frac{\varepsilon}{2}+\left(1-\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}(C), so

Reg⁡(πβχ)\displaystyle\mathrm{Reg}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}) =v⁡(C)−Rr⋆​(πβχ)\displaystyle=v(C)-R^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}) (278)
=(1−α2+ε2)−(ε2+(1−α2)​πβχ​(C))\displaystyle=\left(1-\frac{\alpha}{2}+\frac{\varepsilon}{2}\right)-\left(\frac{\varepsilon}{2}+\left(1-\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}(C)\right) (279)
=(1−α2)​(1−πβχ​(C))\displaystyle=\left(1-\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)\left(1-\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}(C)\right) (280)
=(1−α2)​[εα+ε​δβ​(1−εα)],\displaystyle=\left(1-\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)\Bigg[\frac{\varepsilon}{\alpha}+\frac{\varepsilon\delta}{\beta}\left(1-\frac{\varepsilon}{\alpha}\right)\Bigg], (281)

where in the last line we used πβχ​(C)=(1−ε/α)​(1−ε​δ/β)\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}(C)=\left(1-\varepsilon/\alpha\right)\left(1-\varepsilon\delta/\beta\right) (from (251)). In particular, comparing to (274),

Reg⁡(πβχ)=(1−α2)​εα⏟=Reg⁡(πM)+(1−α2)⋅ε​δβ​(1−εα).\displaystyle\mathrm{Reg}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta})=\underbrace{\left(1-\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)\frac{\varepsilon}{\alpha}}_{=\,\mathrm{Reg}(\pi_{M})}\;+\;\left(1-\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)\cdot\frac{\varepsilon\delta}{\beta}\left(1-\frac{\varepsilon}{\alpha}\right). (282)

The second term above is the additional penalty induced by χ2\chi^{2} tilting: even though πM\pi_{M} only needs to include a (1−α/2)⋅ε/α(1-\alpha/2)\cdot\varepsilon/\alpha fraction of the poisoned spike PP, the χ2\chi^{2} solution incurs an extra loss proportional to the score gap δ\delta and inversely proportional to the regularization parameter β\beta, matching our intuition in the hard instance setup.

Regime III (β>μ\beta>\mu). Although we already showed how to calculate the win-rate in this regime in (266), we will now show a simpler method that is more amenable to our casework. In this regime we have λ=μ−β<0\lambda=\mu-\beta<0, hence for all y∈{B,C,P}y\in\{B,C,P\},

wβ​(y)=r^​(y)−λβ=r^​(y)−(μ−β)β=1+r^​(y)−μβ,\displaystyle w_{\beta}(y)=\frac{\widehat{r}(y)-\lambda}{\beta}=\frac{\widehat{r}(y)-(\mu-\beta)}{\beta}=1+\frac{\widehat{r}(y)-\mu}{\beta}, (283)

and therefore

πβχ​(y)=πref​(y)​wβ​(y)=πref​(y)​(1+r^​(y)−μβ).\displaystyle\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}(y)=\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(y)\,w_{\beta}(y)=\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(y)\left(1+\frac{\widehat{r}(y)-\mu}{\beta}\right). (284)

Plugging π=πβχ\pi=\pi^{\chi}_{\beta} into the win-rate formula in (260) gives

Rr⋆​(πβχ)\displaystyle R^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}) =∑tπref​(t)​(1+r^​(t)−μβ)​v​(t)\displaystyle=\sum_{t}\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(t)\left(1+\frac{\widehat{r}(t)-\mu}{\beta}\right)v(t) (285)
=∑tπref​(t)​v​(t)⏟=Rr⋆​(πref)+1β∑tπref​(t)​(r^​(t)−μ)​v​(t)⏟=:S⁡(α,ε,δ).\displaystyle=\underbrace{\sum_{t}\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(t)v(t)}_{=R^{r^{\star}}(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})}+\frac{1}{\beta}\underbrace{\sum_{t}\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}(t)\left(\widehat{r}(t)-\mu\right)v(t)}_{=:S(\alpha,\varepsilon,\delta)}. (286)

where the constant S⁡(α,ε,δ)S(\alpha,\varepsilon,\delta) depends only on the instance (and not on β\beta). Indeed, one can easily verify this by rearranging (266). Thus, for β>μ\beta>\mu,

Rr⋆​(πβχ)=Rr⋆​(πref)+S⁡(α,ε,δ)β,\displaystyle R^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta})=R^{r^{\star}}(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})+\frac{S(\alpha,\varepsilon,\delta)}{\beta}, (287)

Consequently, using the regret definition (273) with benchmark v⁡(C)v(C), for all β>μ\beta>\mu,

Reg⁡(πβχ)=v⁡(C)−Rr⋆​(πref)−S⁡(α,ε,δ)β,\displaystyle\mathrm{Reg}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta})=v(C)-R^{r^{\star}}(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})-\frac{S(\alpha,\varepsilon,\delta)}{\beta}, (288)

which is affine in 1/β1/\beta.

Comparing regrets across regimes.

Recall from (274) that

Reg⁡(πM)=(1−α2)​εα,\displaystyle\mathrm{Reg}(\pi_{M})=\left(1-\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)\frac{\varepsilon}{\alpha}, (289)

and from (273) that Reg⁡(π)=v⁡(C)−Rr⋆​(π)\mathrm{Reg}(\pi)=v(C)-R^{r^{\star}}(\pi) with v⁡(C)=1−α−ε2v(C)=1-\frac{\alpha-\varepsilon}{2}. We will now lower bound infβ>0Reg⁡(πβχ)\inf_{\beta>0}\mathrm{Reg}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}) by analyzing each β\beta-regime.

Regime I (β≤ε​δ\beta\leq\varepsilon\delta). From (277), Reg⁡(πβχ)=1−α2\mathrm{Reg}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta})=1-\frac{\alpha}{2}. Using α=k​ε\alpha=k\sqrt{\varepsilon} and ε≤14​k2\varepsilon\leq\frac{1}{4k^{2}}, we have

εα=εk≤12​k2.\displaystyle\frac{\varepsilon}{\alpha}=\frac{\sqrt{\varepsilon}}{k}\ \leq\ \frac{1}{2k^{2}}. (290)

Plugging into (289) yields

Reg⁡(πM)=(1−α2)​εα≤(1−α2)​12​k2.\displaystyle\mathrm{Reg}(\pi_{M})=\left(1-\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)\frac{\varepsilon}{\alpha}\ \leq\ \left(1-\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)\frac{1}{2k^{2}}. (291)

Therefore,

Reg⁡(πβχ)=1−α2≥ 2​k2​Reg​(πM)≥c​Reg​(πM),\displaystyle\mathrm{Reg}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta})=1-\frac{\alpha}{2}\ \geq\ 2k^{2}\,\mathrm{Reg}(\pi_{M})\ \geq\ c\,\mathrm{Reg}(\pi_{M}), (292)

since k2≥2​ck^{2}\geq 2c.

Regime II (ε​δ<β≤μ\varepsilon\delta<\beta\leq\mu). From (278),

Reg⁡(πβχ)=(1−α2)​[εα+ε​δβ​(1−εα)],\displaystyle\mathrm{Reg}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta})=\left(1-\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)\Bigg[\frac{\varepsilon}{\alpha}+\frac{\varepsilon\delta}{\beta}\left(1-\frac{\varepsilon}{\alpha}\right)\Bigg], (293)

which is decreasing in β\beta, hence minimized at β=μ\beta=\mu:

infε​δ<β≤μReg⁡(πβχ)=Reg⁡(πμχ)=(1−α2)​εμ.\displaystyle\inf_{\varepsilon\delta<\beta\leq\mu}\mathrm{Reg}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta})=\mathrm{Reg}(\pi^{\chi}_{\mu})=\left(1-\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)\frac{\varepsilon}{\mu}. (294)

Dividing by (289) gives

Reg⁡(πμχ)Reg⁡(πM)=αμ=1(1−δ)+δ​ε/α.\displaystyle\frac{\mathrm{Reg}(\pi^{\chi}_{\mu})}{\mathrm{Reg}(\pi_{M})}=\frac{\alpha}{\mu}=\frac{1}{(1-\delta)+\delta\,\varepsilon/\alpha}. (295)

Using ε/α=ε/k≤12​k2\varepsilon/\alpha=\sqrt{\varepsilon}/k\leq\frac{1}{2k^{2}} (from ε≤14​k2\varepsilon\leq\frac{1}{4k^{2}}),

(1−δ)+δ​ε/α≤(1−δ)+δ2​k2≤12​c+14​c=34​c≤1c,\displaystyle(1-\delta)+\delta\,\varepsilon/\alpha\ \leq\ (1-\delta)+\frac{\delta}{2k^{2}}\ \leq\ \frac{1}{2c}+\frac{1}{4c}\ =\ \frac{3}{4c}\ \leq\ \frac{1}{c}, (296)

where we used δ≥1−12​c\delta\geq 1-\frac{1}{2c} and k2≥2​ck^{2}\geq 2c in the second inequality. Plugging into (295) yields Reg⁡(πμχ)≥c​Reg​(πM)\mathrm{Reg}(\pi^{\chi}_{\mu})\geq c\,\mathrm{Reg}(\pi_{M}). Since Reg⁡(πβχ)\mathrm{Reg}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}) is decreasing in β\beta on Regime II, for all β∈(ε​δ,μ]\beta\in(\varepsilon\delta,\mu] we have

Reg⁡(πβχ)≥Reg⁡(πμχ)≥c​Reg​(πM).\displaystyle\mathrm{Reg}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta})\ \geq\ \mathrm{Reg}(\pi^{\chi}_{\mu})\ \geq\ c\,\mathrm{Reg}(\pi_{M}). (297)

Regime III (β>μ\beta>\mu). From (288),

Reg⁡(πβχ)=v⁡(C)−Rr⋆​(πref)−S⁡(α,ε,δ)β,\displaystyle\mathrm{Reg}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta})=v(C)-R^{r^{\star}}(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})-\frac{S(\alpha,\varepsilon,\delta)}{\beta}, (298)

so Reg⁡(πβχ)\mathrm{Reg}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta}) is affine in 1/β1/\beta over β>μ\beta>\mu. Hence the minimum over β>μ\beta>\mu is attained at an endpoint:

infβ>μReg⁡(πβχ)=min⁡{Reg⁡(πμχ),Reg⁡(πref)}.\displaystyle\inf_{\beta>\mu}\mathrm{Reg}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta})=\min\Big\{\mathrm{Reg}(\pi^{\chi}_{\mu}),\ \mathrm{Reg}(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})\Big\}. (299)

The first endpoint Reg⁡(πμχ)\mathrm{Reg}(\pi^{\chi}_{\mu}) is already lower bounded by c​Reg​(πM)c\,\mathrm{Reg}(\pi_{M}) from Regime II. It remains to lower bound the second endpoint, which is Reg⁡(πref)\mathrm{Reg}(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}). Under the half-ties convention, by symmetry of i.i.d. draws,

Rr⋆​(πref)=ℙy,y′∼πref​(r⋆​(y)>r⋆​(y′))+12​ℙy,y′∼πref​(r⋆​(y)=r⋆​(y′))=12.\displaystyle R^{r^{\star}}(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})=\mathbb{P}_{y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}\left(r^{\star}(y)>r^{\star}(y^{\prime})\right)+\frac{1}{2}\mathbb{P}_{y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}\left(r^{\star}(y)=r^{\star}(y^{\prime})\right)=\frac{1}{2}. (300)

Therefore,

Reg⁡(πref)=v⁡(C)−Rr⋆​(πref)=(1−α−ε2)−12=1−α+ε2≥14,\displaystyle\mathrm{Reg}(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})=v(C)-R^{r^{\star}}(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})=\left(1-\frac{\alpha-\varepsilon}{2}\right)-\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1-\alpha+\varepsilon}{2}\geq\frac{1}{4}, (301)

where the last inequality follows from α≤12\alpha\leq\tfrac{1}{2} by construction. On the other hand, using ε/α≤12​k2\varepsilon/\alpha\leq\frac{1}{2k^{2}} again,

Reg⁡(πM)=(1−α2)​εα≤εα≤12​k2≤14​c,\displaystyle\mathrm{Reg}(\pi_{M})=\left(1-\frac{\alpha}{2}\right)\frac{\varepsilon}{\alpha}\leq\frac{\varepsilon}{\alpha}\leq\frac{1}{2k^{2}}\leq\frac{1}{4c}, (302)

where the last inequality uses k2≥2​ck^{2}\geq 2c. Hence Reg⁡(πref)≥14≥c​Reg​(πM)\mathrm{Reg}(\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})\geq\frac{1}{4}\geq c\,\mathrm{Reg}(\pi_{M}). Plugging into (299) gives Reg⁡(πβχ)≥c​Reg​(πM)\mathrm{Reg}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta})\geq c\,\mathrm{Reg}(\pi_{M}) for all β>μ\beta>\mu.

Concluding the separation. Combining the three regimes yields

infβ>0Rr⋆​(π⋆)−Rr⋆​(πβχ)≥c⋅(infM>0Rr⋆​(π⋆)−Rr⋆​(πM)),\displaystyle\inf_{\beta>0}R^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\star})-R^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\chi}_{\beta})\geq c\cdot\left(\inf_{M>0}R^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\star})-R^{r^{\star}}(\pi_{M})\right), (303)

as claimed. ∎

Appendix E Proofs under win-rate against an arbitrary comparison policy

In this section, we provide proofs for the upper bounds on the performance of BoN and ℰM\mathcal{E}_{M}-regularized BoN when win-rate is compared against an arbitrary measure qq. This section is organized as follows:

  1. 1.

    Section E.1 provides a modified win-rate transfer lemma introduced in Appendix B under win-rate against πref\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}, under a bounded density ratio assumption between qq and πref\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}.

  2. 2.

    Section E.2 provides a general upper bound on the regret of BoN in terms of the ℰM\mathcal{E}_{M}-divergence introduced in Section 2.3, with a new baseline comparator policy for win-rate.

  3. 3.

    In Section E.3, we give a general upper bound on the regret of our implementation of the ℰM\mathcal{E}_{M}-regularized BoN policy under the win-rate against an arbitrary qq.

Before proceeding to the proofs, recall from Section 6 that we defined the win-rate against qq by

Rqr(π):=𝔼y∼π,y′∼q[ϕr(y,y′)]andϕr(y,y′):=𝟏{r(y)>r(y′)}+12 1{r(y)=r(y′)}.\displaystyle R^{r}_{q}(\pi)\;:=\;\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\pi,\;y^{\prime}\sim q}\!\left[\phi_{r}(y,y^{\prime})\right]\quad\text{and}\quad\phi_{r}(y,y^{\prime}):=\mathbf{1}\{r(y)>r(y^{\prime})\}+\tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathbf{1}\{r(y)=r(y^{\prime})\}. (304)

This definition generalizes the win-rate definition against πref\pi_{\mathrm{ref}} in Equation 2, where we now draw y′∼qy^{\prime}\sim q to compare against a random sample from our policy. We will assume throughout this section that q≪πrefq\ll\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}, and

wq​(y):=d​qd​πref​(y)≤Lπref​-a.s.\displaystyle w_{q}(y):=\frac{dq}{d\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}(y)\leq L\qquad\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}\text{-a.s.} (305)

for some constant L≥1L\geq 1. We continue to measure pairwise reward-model error with respect to πref\pi_{\mathrm{ref}} via

εpw​(r^)=𝔼y,y′∼πref​[|ϕr^​(y,y′)−ϕr⋆​(y,y′)|].\displaystyle\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}}(\widehat{r})\;=\;\mathbb{E}_{y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}\!\left[\left|\phi_{\widehat{r}}(y,y^{\prime})-\phi_{r^{\star}}(y,y^{\prime})\right|\right]. (306)

E.1 Transfer lemma for win-rate against qq

Lemma 12 (Win-rate transfer against qq).

Fix πref\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}, qq satisfying (305), a true reward r⋆r^{\star}, and a learned reward model r^\widehat{r}. For any policy π≪πref\pi\ll\pi_{\mathrm{ref}} with density ratio wπ:=d​π/d​πrefw_{\pi}:=d\pi/d\pi_{\mathrm{ref}} and any M≥1M\geq 1,

|Rqr⋆(π)−Rqr^(π)|≤L(M⋅εpw(r^)+ℰM(π∥πref)),\displaystyle\left|R^{r^{\star}}_{q}(\pi)-R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi)\right|\;\leq\;L\left(M\cdot\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}}(\widehat{r})+\mathcal{E}_{M}(\pi\|\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})\right), (307)

where ℰM(π∥πref):=𝔼y∼πref[(wπ(y)−M)+]\mathcal{E}_{M}(\pi\|\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}):=\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}[(w_{\pi}(y)-M)_{+}].

Proof.

The proof follows the same strategy as Lemma 4. We first define ℓ⁡(y,y′):=|ϕr⋆​(y,y′)−ϕr^​(y,y′)|∈[0,1]\ell(y,y^{\prime}):=|\phi_{r^{\star}}(y,y^{\prime})-\phi_{\widehat{r}}(y,y^{\prime})|\in[0,1]. Then

|Rqr⋆​(π)−Rqr^​(π)|\displaystyle\left|R^{r^{\star}}_{q}(\pi)-R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi)\right| =|𝔼y∼π,y′∼q​[ϕr⋆​(y,y′)−ϕr^​(y,y′)]|\displaystyle=\left|\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\pi,\;y^{\prime}\sim q}\!\left[\phi_{r^{\star}}(y,y^{\prime})-\phi_{\widehat{r}}(y,y^{\prime})\right]\right| (308)
≤𝔼y∼π,y′∼q​[ℓ⁡(y,y′)].\displaystyle\leq\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\pi,\;y^{\prime}\sim q}\!\left[\ell(y,y^{\prime})\right]. (309)

We can then perform a change of measure using wπ=d​π/d​πrefw_{\pi}=d\pi/d\pi_{\mathrm{ref}} and wq=d​q/d​πrefw_{q}=dq/d\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}:

𝔼y∼π,y′∼q​[ℓ⁡(y,y′)]=𝔼y,y′∼πref​[wπ​(y)​wq​(y′)​ℓ​(y,y′)]≤L⋅𝔼y,y′∼πref​[wπ​(y)​ℓ​(y,y′)],\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\pi,\;y^{\prime}\sim q}\!\left[\ell(y,y^{\prime})\right]=\mathbb{E}_{y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}\!\left[w_{\pi}(y)\,w_{q}(y^{\prime})\,\ell(y,y^{\prime})\right]\leq L\cdot\mathbb{E}_{y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}\!\left[w_{\pi}(y)\,\ell(y,y^{\prime})\right], (310)

where the inequality uses wq≤Lw_{q}\leq L πref\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}-a.s. Now decompose wπ​(y)=(wπ​(y)∧M)+(wπ​(y)−M)+w_{\pi}(y)=(w_{\pi}(y)\wedge M)+(w_{\pi}(y)-M)_{+} and use ℓ∈[0,1]\ell\in[0,1]:

𝔼y,y′∼πref​[wπ​(y)​ℓ​(y,y′)]\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}\!\left[w_{\pi}(y)\,\ell(y,y^{\prime})\right] =𝔼y,y′∼πref​[(wπ​(y)∧M)​ℓ​(y,y′)]+𝔼y,y′∼πref​[(wπ​(y)−M)+​ℓ​(y,y′)]\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}\!\left[(w_{\pi}(y)\wedge M)\,\ell(y,y^{\prime})\right]+\mathbb{E}_{y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}\!\left[(w_{\pi}(y)-M)_{+}\,\ell(y,y^{\prime})\right] (311)
≤M⋅𝔼y,y′∼πref​[ℓ⁡(y,y′)]+𝔼y∼πref​[(wπ​(y)−M)+]\displaystyle\leq M\cdot\mathbb{E}_{y,y^{\prime}\sim\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}\!\left[\ell(y,y^{\prime})\right]+\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}\!\left[(w_{\pi}(y)-M)_{+}\right] (312)
=M⋅εpw(r^)+ℰM(π∥πref).\displaystyle=M\cdot\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}}(\widehat{r})+\mathcal{E}_{M}(\pi\|\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}). (313)

Multiplying by LL yields (307). ∎

E.2 Proof of Theorem 6

Next, we provide a proof of the upper bound on the regret of the BoN policy when win-rate is comparing against an arbitrary measure qq. Optimizing the following bound in the same way that we did for the πref\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}-win-rate case yields the same result as Theorem 3 up to constant factors.

Theorem 9.

Under the pointwise bound on the density ratio of qq in (305), for any N≥1N\geq 1, reference model πref\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}, comparator π⋆≪πref\pi^{\star}\ll\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}, ground truth reward r⋆r^{\star}, and learned reward model r^\widehat{r}, it holds that

Rqr⋆(π⋆)−Rqr⋆(π^BoN)≲L⋅N⋅εpw(r^)⋅log(1/εpw​(r^))+ℰN/log⁡(1/εpw​(r^))(π⋆∥πref).\displaystyle R_{q}^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\star})-R_{q}^{r^{\star}}(\widehat{\pi}_{\mathrm{BoN}})\lesssim L\cdot N\cdot\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}}(\widehat{r})\cdot\log\left(\nicefrac{{1}}{{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}}(\widehat{r})}}\right)+\mathcal{E}_{N/\log(1/\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}}(\widehat{r}))}\left(\pi^{\star}\|\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}\right). (314)
Proof.

We follow the proof of Theorem 3 detailed in Section C.1, replacing R(⋅)R^{(\cdot)} with Rq(⋅)R^{(\cdot)}_{q}. In particular, for any M>0M>0, the same regret decomposition holds:

Rqr⋆​(π⋆)−Rqr⋆​(π^BoN)=Rqr⋆​(π⋆)−Rqr^​(πM⋆)⏟(T1)+Rqr^​(πM⋆)−Rqr^​(π^BoN)⏟(T2)+Rqr^​(π^BoN)−Rqr⋆​(π^BoN)⏟(T3),\displaystyle R_{q}^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\star})-R_{q}^{r^{\star}}(\widehat{\pi}_{\mathrm{BoN}})=\underbrace{R_{q}^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\star})-R_{q}^{\widehat{r}}(\pi^{\star}_{M})}_{\mathrm{(T1)}}+\underbrace{R_{q}^{\widehat{r}}(\pi^{\star}_{M})-R_{q}^{\widehat{r}}(\widehat{\pi}_{\mathrm{BoN}})}_{\mathrm{(T2)}}+\underbrace{R_{q}^{\widehat{r}}(\widehat{\pi}_{\mathrm{BoN}})-R_{q}^{r^{\star}}(\widehat{\pi}_{\mathrm{BoN}})}_{\mathrm{(T3)}}, (315)

where πM⋆\pi^{\star}_{M} is the same MM-capped TV projection defined in (96). To bound (T1)\mathrm{(T1)}, we decompose as in Section C.1:

Rqr⋆​(π⋆)−Rqr^​(πM⋆)=Rqr⋆​(π⋆)−Rqr⋆​(πM⋆)+Rqr⋆​(πM⋆)−Rqr^​(πM⋆).\displaystyle R_{q}^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\star})-R_{q}^{\widehat{r}}(\pi^{\star}_{M})=R_{q}^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\star})-R_{q}^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\star}_{M})+R_{q}^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\star}_{M})-R_{q}^{\widehat{r}}(\pi^{\star}_{M}). (316)

The first difference is controlled exactly as before: for fixed (r,q)(r,q), the win-rate functional is bounded and therefore 11-Lipschitz in total variation. Thus,

Rqr⋆(π⋆)−Rqr⋆(πM⋆)≤TV(π⋆,πM⋆)=ℰM(π⋆∥πref),\displaystyle R_{q}^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\star})-R_{q}^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\star}_{M})\leq\mathrm{TV}(\pi^{\star},\pi^{\star}_{M})=\mathcal{E}_{M}(\pi^{\star}\|\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}), (317)

where the equality uses the same arguments from Block and Polyanskiy [2] as in the proof of Theorem 3. For the second difference, apply Lemma 12 with π=πM⋆\pi=\pi^{\star}_{M}; since d​πM⋆/d​πref≤M\nicefrac{{d\pi^{\star}_{M}}}{{d\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}}\leq M, we have ℰM(πM⋆∥πref)=0\mathcal{E}_{M}(\pi^{\star}_{M}\|\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})=0, and thus

Rqr⋆​(πM⋆)−Rqr^​(πM⋆)≤L⋅M​εpw​(r^).\displaystyle R_{q}^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\star}_{M})-R_{q}^{\widehat{r}}(\pi^{\star}_{M})\leq L\cdot M\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}}(\widehat{r}). (318)

Therefore,

(T1)≤ℰM(π⋆∥πref)+LMεpw(r^).\displaystyle\mathrm{(T1)}\leq\mathcal{E}_{M}(\pi^{\star}\|\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})+L\,M\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}}(\widehat{r}). (319)

Next, in order to bound (T2)\mathrm{(T2)}, we introduce the same approximate rejection sampling selection rule πM,rej⋆\pi^{\star}_{M,\mathrm{rej}} as in Section C.1 and decompose

Rqr^​(πM⋆)−Rqr^​(π^BoN)=Rqr^​(πM⋆)−Rqr^​(πM,rej⋆)+Rqr^​(πM,rej⋆)−Rqr^​(π^BoN).\displaystyle R_{q}^{\widehat{r}}(\pi^{\star}_{M})-R_{q}^{\widehat{r}}(\widehat{\pi}_{\mathrm{BoN}})=R_{q}^{\widehat{r}}(\pi^{\star}_{M})-R_{q}^{\widehat{r}}(\pi^{\star}_{M,\mathrm{rej}})+R_{q}^{\widehat{r}}(\pi^{\star}_{M,\mathrm{rej}})-R_{q}^{\widehat{r}}(\widehat{\pi}_{\mathrm{BoN}}). (320)

The first difference is controlled exactly as before by the approximate rejection sampling analysis of Block and Polyanskiy [2], using only boundedness of win-rate:

Rqr^(πM⋆)−Rqr^(πM,rej⋆)≤TV(πM⋆,πM,rej⋆)≤12exp(−N/M),\displaystyle R_{q}^{\widehat{r}}(\pi^{\star}_{M})-R_{q}^{\widehat{r}}(\pi^{\star}_{M,\mathrm{rej}})\leq\mathrm{TV}(\pi^{\star}_{M},\pi^{\star}_{M,\mathrm{rej}})\leq\tfrac{1}{2}\exp(-N/M), (321)

since ℰM(πM⋆∥πref)=0\mathcal{E}_{M}(\pi^{\star}_{M}\|\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})=0. For the second difference, conditional on any fixed batch 𝒴^N=(y1,…,yN)\widehat{\mathcal{Y}}_{N}=(y_{1},\dots,y_{N}), BoN outputs an index attaining maxi⁡r^​(yi)\max_{i}\widehat{r}(y_{i}). We define

gr,q​(r⁡(y)):=ℙy′∼q​(r⁡(y′)<r⁡(y))+12​ℙy′∼q​(r⁡(y′)=r⁡(y))∈[0,1],\displaystyle g_{r,q}(r(y)):=\mathbb{P}_{y^{\prime}\sim q}\left(r(y^{\prime})<r(y)\right)+\tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathbb{P}_{y^{\prime}\sim q}\left(r(y^{\prime})=r(y)\right)\in[0,1], (322)

so that for any policy π\pi, Rqr^​(π)=𝔼y∼π​[gr^,q​(r^​(y))]R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi)=\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\pi}[g_{\widehat{r},q}(\widehat{r}(y))] by conditioning on yy exactly as in Lemma 5. From this, it is clear that gr^,qg_{\widehat{r},q} is nondecreasing in r^​(y)\widehat{r}(y). Therefore, for any y∈𝒴^Ny\in\widehat{\mathcal{Y}}_{N} we have gr^,q​(r^​(y))≤maxi∈[N]⁡gr^,q​(r^​(yi))g_{\widehat{r},q}(\widehat{r}(y))\leq\max_{i\in[N]}g_{\widehat{r},q}(\widehat{r}(y_{i})), and the same coupling argument as in the proof of Theorem 3 gives

Rqr^​(πM,rej⋆)−Rqr^​(π^BoN)≤0.\displaystyle R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi^{\star}_{M,\mathrm{rej}})-R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\widehat{\pi}_{\mathrm{BoN}})\leq 0. (323)

Combining the bounds on the two differences ensures

(T2)≤12exp(−N/M).\displaystyle\mathrm{(T2)}\leq\tfrac{1}{2}\exp(-N/M). (324)

To bound (T3)\mathrm{(T3)}, recall that in Section C.1 we showed that BoN satisfies d​π^BoN/d​πref≤N\nicefrac{{d\widehat{\pi}_{\mathrm{BoN}}}}{{d\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}}\leq N pointwise, so ℰN(π^BoN∥πref)=0\mathcal{E}_{N}(\widehat{\pi}_{\mathrm{BoN}}\|\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})=0. Applying Lemma 12 with π=π^BoN\pi=\widehat{\pi}_{\mathrm{BoN}} and truncation M=NM=N yields

(T3)=Rqr^​(π^BoN)−Rqr⋆​(π^BoN)≤L⋅N​εpw​(r^).\displaystyle\mathrm{(T3)}=R_{q}^{\widehat{r}}(\widehat{\pi}_{\mathrm{BoN}})-R_{q}^{r^{\star}}(\widehat{\pi}_{\mathrm{BoN}})\leq L\cdot N\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}}(\widehat{r}). (325)

Combining (319), (324), and (325) with (315) gives

Rqr⋆(π⋆)−Rqr⋆(π^BoN)≲ℰM(π⋆∥πref)+L(M+N)εpw(r^)+exp(−N/M).\displaystyle R_{q}^{r^{\star}}(\pi^{\star})-R_{q}^{r^{\star}}(\widehat{\pi}_{\mathrm{BoN}})\;\lesssim\;\mathcal{E}_{M}(\pi^{\star}\|\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})+L(M+N)\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}}(\widehat{r})+\exp(-N/M). (326)

Setting M=N/log⁡(1/εpw​(r^))M=N/\log\left(\nicefrac{{1}}{{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}}(\widehat{r})}}\right) and observing that for such MM, it holds that exp(−N/M)=εpw(r^)\exp(-N/M)=\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}}(\widehat{r}), we obtain the desired result. ∎

E.3 Proof of Theorem 7

Finally, we provide an upper bound on the regret of the ℰM\mathcal{E}_{M}-regularized BoN policy when win-rate is comparing against an arbitrary measure qq. We again work under the assumption that the density ratio of π^M\widehat{\pi}_{M} is bounded pointwise (305). Note that while the following bound is qualitatively similar to the result from Theorem 3, we obtain a slower rate in NN while staying minimax optimal.

Theorem 10.

For any M,N≥1M,N\geq 1, reference model πref\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}, comparator π⋆≪πref\pi^{\star}\ll\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}, ground truth reward r⋆r^{\star}, and learned reward model r^\widehat{r}, it holds that

Rqr⋆(π⋆)−Rqr⋆(π^M)≲L⋅ℰM(π⋆∥πref)+L⋅M⋅εpw(r^)+MN.\displaystyle R^{r^{\star}}_{q}(\pi^{\star})-R^{r^{\star}}_{q}(\widehat{\pi}_{M})\lesssim L\cdot\mathcal{E}_{M}(\pi^{\star}\|\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})+L\cdot M\cdot\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}}(\widehat{r})+\sqrt{\frac{M}{N}}. (327)
Proof.

Fix M≥1M\geq 1 and let k:=⌈N/M⌉k:=\lceil N/M\rceil. Recall that π^M\widehat{\pi}_{M} is the (unconditional) law of the random output youty_{\mathrm{out}} produced by: sample y1,…,yN​∼iid​πrefy_{1},\dots,y_{N}\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}\pi_{\mathrm{ref}} and i.i.d. V1,…,VN∼Unif⁡[0,1]V_{1},\dots,V_{N}\sim{\rm Unif}[0,1] independent; let II index the top-kk samples under the lexicographic order (r^​(yi),Vi)(\widehat{r}(y_{i}),V_{i}); output yJy_{J} with JJ uniform on II conditional on (𝒴^N,V1:N)(\widehat{\mathcal{Y}}_{N},V_{1:N}). As in the proof of Theorem 5 with πref\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}-win-rate, we consider the same regret decomposition:

Rqr⋆​(π⋆)−Rqr⋆​(π^M)\displaystyle R^{r^{\star}}_{q}(\pi^{\star})-R^{r^{\star}}_{q}(\widehat{\pi}_{M}) =(Rqr⋆​(π⋆)−Rqr^​(πM⋆))⏟(T1)+(Rqr^​(πM⋆)−Rqr^​(π^M))⏟(T2)+(Rqr^​(π^M)−Rqr⋆​(π^M))⏟(T3).\displaystyle=\underbrace{\left(R^{r^{\star}}_{q}(\pi^{\star})-R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi^{\star}_{M})\right)}_{\mathrm{(T1)}}+\underbrace{\left(R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi^{\star}_{M})-R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\widehat{\pi}_{M})\right)}_{\mathrm{(T2)}}+\underbrace{\left(R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\widehat{\pi}_{M})-R^{r^{\star}}_{q}(\widehat{\pi}_{M})\right)}_{\mathrm{(T3)}}. (328)

Here, πM⋆\pi^{\star}_{M} is defined exactly as before: it minimizes total variation distance to π⋆\pi^{\star} over all π≪πref\pi\ll\pi_{\mathrm{ref}} such that d​πd​πref≤M\frac{d\pi}{d\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}\leq M πref\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}-a.s. To bound (T1)\mathrm{(T1)}, we decompose

Rqr⋆​(π⋆)−Rqr^​(πM⋆)=Rqr⋆​(π⋆)−Rqr^​(π⋆)+Rqr^​(π⋆)−Rqr^​(πM⋆).\displaystyle R^{r^{\star}}_{q}(\pi^{\star})-R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi^{\star}_{M})=R^{r^{\star}}_{q}(\pi^{\star})-R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi^{\star})+R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi^{\star})-R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi^{\star}_{M}). (329)

For the first difference, we apply Lemma 12 to obtain

Rqr⋆(π⋆)−Rqr^(π⋆)≤L(Mεpw(r^)+ℰM(π⋆∥πref)).\displaystyle R^{r^{\star}}_{q}(\pi^{\star})-R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi^{\star})\;\leq\;L\left(M\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}}(\widehat{r})+\mathcal{E}_{M}(\pi^{\star}\|\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})\right). (330)

For the second difference, we observe that for fixed (q,r^)(q,\widehat{r}) the win-rate functional is bounded and therefore 11-Lipschitz in total variation. Thus,

Rqr^(π⋆)−Rqr^(πM⋆)≤TV(π⋆,πM⋆)=ℰM(π⋆∥πref),\displaystyle R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi^{\star})-R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi^{\star}_{M})\leq\mathrm{TV}(\pi^{\star},\pi^{\star}_{M})=\mathcal{E}_{M}(\pi^{\star}\|\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}), (331)

where the last equality uses the same approximate rejection sampling arguments from Block and Polyanskiy [2] as before. Combining,

(T1)≲LℰM(π⋆∥πref)+LMεpw(r^).\displaystyle\mathrm{(T1)}\;\lesssim\;L\,\mathcal{E}_{M}(\pi^{\star}\|\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})\;+\;L\,M\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}}(\widehat{r}). (332)

For (T2)\mathrm{(T2)}, as before, we introduce the ideal top-1/M1/M threshold policy

πM(⋅):=πref(⋅∣r^(⋅)≥λM),\displaystyle\pi_{M}(\cdot):=\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}\left(\cdot\mid\widehat{r}(\cdot)\geq\lambda_{M}\right), (333)

so that ℙy∼πref​(r^​(y)≥λM)=1M\mathbb{P}_{y\sim\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}}\left(\widehat{r}(y)\geq\lambda_{M}\right)=\frac{1}{M}, and we decompose as

Rqr^​(πM⋆)−Rqr^​(π^M)=Rqr^​(πM⋆)−Rqr^​(πM)+Rqr^​(πM)−Rqr^​(π^M).\displaystyle R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi^{\star}_{M})-R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\widehat{\pi}_{M})=R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi^{\star}_{M})-R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi_{M})+R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi_{M})-R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\widehat{\pi}_{M}). (334)

For the first difference, as in the proof of Theorem 9, we define

gr,q​(r⁡(y)):=ℙy′∼q​(r⁡(y)>r⁡(y′))+12​ℙy′∼q​(r⁡(y)=r⁡(y′))∈[0,1],\displaystyle g_{r,q}(r(y)):=\mathbb{P}_{y^{\prime}\sim q}\left(r(y)>r(y^{\prime})\right)+\tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathbb{P}_{y^{\prime}\sim q}\left(r(y)=r(y^{\prime})\right)\in[0,1], (335)

so that for any policy π\pi, Rqr^​(π)=𝔼y∼π​[gr^,q​(r^​(y))]R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi)=\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\pi}[g_{\widehat{r},q}(\widehat{r}(y))] by conditioning on yy exactly as in Lemma 5. From this, it is clear that gr^,qg_{\widehat{r},q} is nondecreasing in r^​(y)\widehat{r}(y), so πM\pi_{M} (output by Proposition 4 with s=r^s=\widehat{r}) maximizes Rqr^​(π)R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi) over the class of policies with density ratio bounded by MM. Recalling that πM⋆\pi^{\star}_{M} is also feasible subject to this constraint, it follows that Rqr^​(πM⋆)≤Rqr^​(πM)R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi^{\star}_{M})\leq R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi_{M}), and hence

Rqr^​(πM⋆)−Rqr^​(πM)≤0.\displaystyle R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi^{\star}_{M})-R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi_{M})\leq 0. (336)

It remains to bound Rqr^​(πM)−Rqr^​(π^M)R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi_{M})-R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\widehat{\pi}_{M}). As in Section D.2, we let Fr^F_{\widehat{r}} and Fr^(⋅−)F_{\widehat{r}}(\cdot^{-}) denote the cumulative density functions of r^​(y)\widehat{r}(y) with y∼πrefy\sim\pi_{\mathrm{ref}} as in Lemma 5, and given an auxiliary seed V∼Unif⁡[0,1]V\sim{\rm Unif}[0,1] independent of yy, we define

u~​(y,V):=Fr^​(r^​(y)−)+V⁡(Fr^​(r^​(y))−Fr^​(r^​(y)−))∈[0,1].\displaystyle\tilde{u}(y;V):=F_{\widehat{r}}(\widehat{r}(y)^{-})+V\left(F_{\widehat{r}}(\widehat{r}(y))-F_{\widehat{r}}(\widehat{r}(y)^{-})\right)\in[0,1]. (337)

By the same uniformization argument as in Lemma 5, u~​(y,V)∼Unif​[0,1]\tilde{u}(y;V)\sim{\rm Unif}[0,1], and moreover

Fr^−1​(u~​(y,V))=r^​(y)\displaystyle F_{\widehat{r}}^{-1}(\tilde{u}(y;V))=\widehat{r}(y) (338)

πref\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}-a.s., where Fr^−1F_{\widehat{r}}^{-1} is the generalized inverse. As in the proof of Theorem 5, ranking by (r^​(yi),Vi)(\widehat{r}(y_{i}),V_{i}) is equivalent to ranking by u~i:=u~​(yi,Vi)\tilde{u}_{i}:=\tilde{u}(y_{i};V_{i}). We let u1,…,uN​∼iid​Unif​[0,1]u_{1},\dots,u_{N}\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}{\rm Unif}[0,1] denote these randomized ranks, and write u(1)≤⋯≤u(N)u_{(1)}\leq\cdots\leq u_{(N)}. Now we set t:=1−1Mt:=1-\frac{1}{M} and define the empirical cutoff τ:=u(N−k)\tau:=u_{(N-k)} (so the selected set corresponds to the top kk ranks). We also define the bounded monotone function

h⁡(u):=gr^,q​(Fr^−1​(u))∈[0,1],\displaystyle h(u):=g_{\widehat{r},q}\!\left(F_{\widehat{r}}^{-1}(u)\right)\in[0,1], (339)

so that Rqr^​(π)=𝔼y∼π​[h⁡(u~​(y,V))]R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi)=\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\pi}[h(\tilde{u}(y;V))]. Under πM\pi_{M}, we have u~​(y,V)∼Unif​[t,1]\tilde{u}(y;V)\sim{\rm Unif}[t,1], and hence

Rqr^​(πM)=μ⁡(t),\displaystyle R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi_{M})=\mu(t), (340)

where μ⁡(s):=𝔼⁡[h⁡(u)∣u≥s]\mu(s):=\mathbb{E}[h(u)\mid u\geq s] and u∼Unif⁡[0,1]u\sim{\rm Unif}[0,1]. Under π^M\widehat{\pi}_{M}, the output rank uoutu_{\rm out} is uniform over the top kk ranks. Following the same logic as Lemma 11, a standard order-statistic property implies that conditional on τ\tau, the multiset of the kk ranks above τ\tau is i.i.d. Unif⁡[τ,1]{\rm Unif}[\tau,1]; therefore uout|τ∼Unif⁡[τ,1]u_{\rm out}\mid\tau\sim{\rm Unif}[\tau,1] and

Rqr^​(π^M)=𝔼⁡[μ⁡(τ)],\displaystyle R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\widehat{\pi}_{M})=\mathbb{E}\left[\mu(\tau)\right], (341)

where the expectation is over the randomness in τ\tau. At this point we have reduced the gap to

Rqr^​(πM)−Rqr^​(π^M)=μ⁡(t)−𝔼⁡[μ⁡(τ)].\displaystyle R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi_{M})-R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\widehat{\pi}_{M})=\mu(t)-\mathbb{E}[\mu(\tau)]. (342)

To upper bound this quantity, we note that it is immediate that

μ⁡(t)−𝔼⁡[μ⁡(τ)]≤𝔼⁡[|μ⁡(t)−μ⁡(τ)|].\displaystyle\mu(t)-\mathbb{E}[\mu(\tau)]\leq\mathbb{E}\left[|\mu(t)-\mu(\tau)|\right]. (343)

Recall μ⁡(s)=𝔼⁡[h⁡(U)∣U≥s]\mu(s)=\mathbb{E}[h(U)\mid U\geq s] with U∼Unif⁡[0,1]U\sim{\rm Unif}[0,1] and h∈[0,1]h\in[0,1]. Equivalently, if we write Ps:=Unif⁡[s,1]P_{s}:={\rm Unif}[s,1], then μ​(s)=𝔼Ps​[h]\mu(s)=\mathbb{E}_{P_{s}}[h]. Hence for any s,s′∈[0,1)s,s^{\prime}\in[0,1),

|μ⁡(s)−μ⁡(s′)|=|𝔼Ps​[h]−𝔼Ps′​[h]|≤TV⁡(Ps,Ps′).\displaystyle|\mu(s)-\mu(s^{\prime})|=\left|\mathbb{E}_{P_{s}}[h]-\mathbb{E}_{P_{s^{\prime}}}[h]\right|\leq\mathrm{TV}(P_{s},P_{s^{\prime}}). (344)

We next show how to bound this total variation distance. Assume wlog s≤s′s\leq s^{\prime}. The corresponding densities are

fs(u)=11−s 1{u∈[s,1]},fs′(u)=11−s′ 1{u∈[s′,1]},\displaystyle f_{s}(u)=\frac{1}{1-s}\,\mathbf{1}\{u\in[s,1]\},\qquad f_{s^{\prime}}(u)=\frac{1}{1-s^{\prime}}\,\mathbf{1}\{u\in[s^{\prime},1]\}, (345)

so

TV⁡(Ps,Ps′)\displaystyle\mathrm{TV}(P_{s},P_{s^{\prime}}) =12​∫01|fs​(u)−fs′​(u)|​𝑑u\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\int_{0}^{1}|f_{s}(u)-f_{s^{\prime}}(u)|\,du (346)
=12​(∫ss′11−s​𝑑u+∫s′1(11−s′−11−s)​𝑑u)\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\left(\int_{s}^{s^{\prime}}\frac{1}{1-s}\,du\;+\;\int_{s^{\prime}}^{1}\left(\frac{1}{1-s^{\prime}}-\frac{1}{1-s}\right)\,du\right) (347)
=12​(s′−s1−s+(1−s′)​(11−s′−11−s))=s′−s1−s.\displaystyle=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{s^{\prime}-s}{1-s}\;+\;(1-s^{\prime})\left(\frac{1}{1-s^{\prime}}-\frac{1}{1-s}\right)\right)=\frac{s^{\prime}-s}{1-s}. (348)

Therefore, for all s,s′∈[0,1)s,s^{\prime}\in[0,1),

|μ⁡(s)−μ⁡(s′)|≤|s−s′|1−min⁡{s,s′}.\displaystyle|\mu(s)-\mu(s^{\prime})|\leq\frac{|s-s^{\prime}|}{1-\min\{s,s^{\prime}\}}. (349)

Applying this with s=ts=t and s′=τs^{\prime}=\tau yields

|μ⁡(t)−μ⁡(τ)|≤|t−τ|1−min⁡{t,τ}≤|t−τ|1−t=M​|t−τ|,\displaystyle|\mu(t)-\mu(\tau)|\leq\frac{|t-\tau|}{1-\min\{t,\tau\}}\leq\frac{|t-\tau|}{1-t}=M\,|t-\tau|, (350)

since t=1−1Mt=1-\frac{1}{M} and min⁡{t,τ}≤t\min\{t,\tau\}\leq t. Hence

Rqr^​(πM)−Rqr^​(π^M)=μ⁡(t)−𝔼⁡[μ⁡(τ)]≤𝔼⁡[|μ⁡(t)−μ⁡(τ)|]≤M​𝔼​[|t−τ|].\displaystyle R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi_{M})-R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\hat{\pi}_{M})=\mu(t)-\mathbb{E}[\mu(\tau)]\leq\mathbb{E}\left[|\mu(t)-\mu(\tau)|\right]\leq M\,\mathbb{E}[|t-\tau|]. (351)

Hence

Rqr^​(πM)−Rqr^​(π^M)≤M​𝔼​[|t−τ|],\displaystyle R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi_{M})-R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\widehat{\pi}_{M})\leq M\mathbb{E}\left[|t-\tau|\right], (352)

and it remains to bound 𝔼⁡[|t−τ|]\mathbb{E}\left[|t-\tau|\right]. Since u1,…,uN​∼iid​Unif​[0,1]u_{1},\dots,u_{N}\overset{\mathrm{iid}}{\sim}{\rm Unif}[0,1], the cutoff τ=u(N−k)\tau=u_{(N-k)} has the Beta law τ∼Beta⁡(N−k,k+1)\tau\sim{\rm Beta}(N-k,\;k+1). In particular,

𝔼⁡[τ]=N−kN+1andVar⁡(τ)=(N−k)​(k+1)(N+1)2​(N+2)≤k+1(N+1)2.\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[\tau]=\frac{N-k}{N+1}\qquad\text{and}\qquad\Var(\tau)=\frac{(N-k)(k+1)}{(N+1)^{2}(N+2)}\;\leq\;\frac{k+1}{(N+1)^{2}}. (353)

We can decompose using the triangle inequality as

𝔼⁡[|t−τ|]≤|t−𝔼⁡[τ]|+𝔼⁡[|τ−𝔼⁡[τ]|],\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[|t-\tau|]\;\leq\;|t-\mathbb{E}[\tau]|+\mathbb{E}[|\tau-\mathbb{E}[\tau]|], (354)

and using Cauchy-Schwarz on the second term, we obtain

|t−𝔼⁡[τ]|+𝔼⁡[|τ−𝔼⁡[τ]|]≤|t−𝔼⁡[τ]|+Var⁡(τ).\displaystyle|t-\mathbb{E}[\tau]|+\mathbb{E}[|\tau-\mathbb{E}[\tau]|]\;\leq\;|t-\mathbb{E}[\tau]|+\sqrt{\Var(\tau)}. (355)

Since t=1−1Mt=1-\tfrac{1}{M} and k=⌈N/M⌉k=\lceil N/M\rceil, one can easily verify that |𝔼⁡[τ]−t|≲1N|\mathbb{E}[\tau]-t|\lesssim\tfrac{1}{N} (due to rounding) and Var⁡(τ)≲1M​N\sqrt{\Var(\tau)}\lesssim\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{MN}}, yielding

𝔼⁡[|t−τ|]≲1N+1M​N.\displaystyle\mathbb{E}[|t-\tau|]\;\lesssim\;\frac{1}{N}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{MN}}. (356)

Combining with (352) gives

Rqr^​(πM)−Rqr^​(π^M)≲M⁡(1N+1M​N)=MN+MN,\displaystyle R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi_{M})-R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\hat{\pi}_{M})\;\lesssim\;M\left(\frac{1}{N}+\frac{1}{\sqrt{MN}}\right)\;=\;\frac{M}{N}+\sqrt{\frac{M}{N}}, (357)

and hence we can conclude that

(T2)=Rqr^​(πM⋆)−Rqr^​(π^M)≲MN+MN,\displaystyle\mathrm{(T2)}=R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi^{\star}_{M})-R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\widehat{\pi}_{M})\;\lesssim\;\frac{M}{N}+\sqrt{\frac{M}{N}}, (358)

where the second term dominates for large NN. For (T3)\mathrm{(T3)}, as in the proof of Theorem 5, we have ℰM(π^M∥πref)=0\mathcal{E}_{M}(\widehat{\pi}_{M}\|\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})=0 since wπ^M≤N/k≤Mw_{\widehat{\pi}_{M}}\leq N/k\leq M πref\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}-a.s. Applying Lemma 12 to π=π^M\pi=\widehat{\pi}_{M} under (305) yields

(T3)=Rqr^(π^M)−Rqr⋆(π^M)≤L(Mεpw(r^)+ℰM(π^M∥πref))=LMεpw(r^).\displaystyle\mathrm{(T3)}=R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\widehat{\pi}_{M})-R^{r^{\star}}_{q}(\widehat{\pi}_{M})\;\leq\;L\left(M\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}}(\widehat{r})+\mathcal{E}_{M}(\widehat{\pi}_{M}\|\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})\right)=L\,M\,\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}}(\widehat{r}). (359)

Finally, combining (332), (358), and (359) gives

Rqr⋆(π⋆)−Rqr⋆(π^M)≲L⋅ℰM(π⋆∥πref)+L⋅M⋅εpw(r^)+MN.\displaystyle R^{r^{\star}}_{q}(\pi^{\star})-R^{r^{\star}}_{q}(\widehat{\pi}_{M})\lesssim L\cdot\mathcal{E}_{M}(\pi^{\star}\|\pi_{\mathrm{ref}})+L\cdot M\cdot\varepsilon_{\mathrm{pw}}(\widehat{r})+\sqrt{\frac{M}{N}}. (360)

∎

While we do not provide a computational lower bound proving that the M/N\sqrt{M/N} estimation term is tight in full generality, this slower rate can be viewed as an artifact of the general-qq setting. The key obstruction is that for general qq the win-rate becomes a generic tail functional of the randomized r^\widehat{r}-rank rather than an explicitly computable linear statistic as in the proof of Theorem 3 in Section C.1. Concretely, we write

Rqr^​(π)=𝔼y∼π,V​[h⁡(u~​(y,V))],h⁡(u):=gr^,q​(Fr^−1​(u))∈[0,1],\displaystyle R^{\widehat{r}}_{q}(\pi)=\mathbb{E}_{y\sim\pi,\,V}\!\big[h(\tilde{u}(y;V))\big],\qquad h(u):=g_{\widehat{r},q}\!\big(F_{\widehat{r}}^{-1}(u)\big)\in[0,1], (361)

where hh is merely bounded (and monotone) under (305). When q=πrefq=\pi_{\mathrm{ref}}, the corresponding transform is linear (indeed h⁡(u)=uh(u)=u), which is why the empirical top-1/M1/M policy admits an exact order-statistics calculation and yields a 1/N1/N term. For general qq, however, the shape of hh near the fixed cutoff t=1−1Mt=1-\tfrac{1}{M} is uncontrolled: hh can place almost all of its variation in an O⁡(1/M)O(1/M) neighborhood of tt. In such worst cases, small fluctuations of the empirical cutoff τ\tau around tt can translate into a sensitivity bound of the form

|μ⁡(t)−μ⁡(τ)|≲M​|t−τ|,\displaystyle|\mu(t)-\mu(\tau)|\;\lesssim\;M\,|t-\tau|, (362)

which holds for all bounded hh and captures the fact that changing the threshold by |t−τ||t-\tau| perturbs a tail of mass 1/M1/M. Since τ\tau fluctuates around tt at scale 𝔼​|t−τ|≍1/M​N\mathbb{E}|t-\tau|\asymp 1/\sqrt{MN} for k≈N/Mk\approx N/M, this leads to an estimation error on the order of M/N\sqrt{M/N} without additional regularity assumptions on qq (equivalently, on hh) beyond (305).
